hazards.description: Damage to or incorrect installation of gas pipework can result in uncontrolled gas escape, creating an explosive atmosphere. Ignition of accumulated gas can cause fatal blast injuries and structural damage over a wide area.
hazards.who_at_risk: Gas operatives, building occupants, emergency services
control_measures: CAT & Genny scan plus hand-dug trial holes to locate all buried gas mains before any mechanical excavation near gas infrastructure.
Permit to Dig required for all excavation within 500mm of known gas main; minimum 2-person working on all gas isolation tasks.
4-gas monitor (O2, LEL, CO, H2S) bump-tested and calibrated (max 6 months) carried by all operatives; monitor alarm thresholds: O2 <19.5%, LEL >10% = evacuate.
All ignition sources (including battery tools, mobile phones, and vehicles) prohibited within 6m of open gas work; no smoking within 10m.
All gas installation work to be carried out exclusively by Gas Safe registered operatives holding the appropriate ACS certification for the work type.
National Gas Emergency Service number (0800 111 999) posted at site entrance and in welfare; operatives briefed on emergency evacuation procedure.
Immediate site evacuation and emergency services notification if LEL alarm activates.
hazards.legislation_ref: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 / GSIUR 1998

hazards.description: MDPE electrofusion and butt-fusion welding generates polymer degradation fumes from heated pipe surfaces. In enclosed or poorly ventilated excavations and valve pits, fume concentrations can build to levels that cause respiratory irritation and sensitisation with repeated exposure.
hazards.who_at_risk: MDPE fusion operative; any operative working in the immediate vicinity of the fusion weld
control_measures: Forced ventilation to be provided in all enclosed or semi-enclosed spaces where MDPE fusion welding is carried out.
Operatives to wear RPE to minimum FFP2 standard during all fusion welding operations.
MDPE fusion welding to be carried out only by operatives holding a current MDPE electrofusion certification.
No welding to be carried out in wet conditions or where electrofusion unit integrity may be compromised by moisture.

hazards.hazard: Pressure test failure and gas release during commissioning
hazards.description: Incorrect test medium, inadequate joint preparation, or failure to establish correct test pressure can result in joint or pipe failure during strength or tightness testing, releasing pressurised gas or causing blast injury.
hazards.who_at_risk: Gas Safe operatives, anyone in the building during test
control_measures: Strength tests to use nitrogen or compressed air ONLY — never natural gas; all personnel to stand clear of joints during pressurisation.
3m exclusion zone around all joints during strength testing; pressure to be applied gradually and monitored remotely where possible.
Gas Safe registered engineer to witness and certify all tightness tests; test results recorded on appropriate gas certification form.
Purging to be carried out strictly per IGEM/UP/1B: purge to atmosphere at appropriate point; 4-gas monitor used throughout purging and commissioning.
hazards.legislation_ref: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 / PSSR 2000

hazards.hazard: Purging and commissioning — gas release risk
hazards.description: During purging, live natural gas is introduced into the newly installed pipework and displaces air or inert test gas to atmosphere. If the purge point is inadequately ventilated or ignition sources are present, an explosive gas-air mixture can form. Commissioning activities carry the same risk until all joints have been verified leak-free under live pressure.
hazards.who_at_risk: Gas Safe commissioning operative; any operatives or members of the public within the purge exclusion zone
control_measures: Purging and commissioning to be carried out by Gas Safe registered operative holding current ACS certification for the relevant work category.
All ignition sources to be eliminated from the work area before purging commences; no open flames, electrical switching, or smoking within 6m.
4-gas monitor (O2, LEL, CO, H2S) to be in continuous use throughout purging and commissioning operations.
Purging procedure to follow IGEM/UP/1 requirements; all purge records to be retained as part of Gas Safe certification paperwork.
hazards.legislation_ref: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 / IGE/UP/1

legislation.relevance: All gas installation work by Gas Safe registered engineer only. Pipework must be tested and purged in accordance with IGE/UP/1.
Governs conveyance of gas through pipes, emergency procedures, and mandatory reporting of gas escapes.
Covers design, construction, and operation of gas mains and pipelines.
Steel and PE pipework design and installation requirements for gas distribution systems.
Strength and tightness testing procedures for gas installations — all test results to be certified.

method_steps.title: CAT Scan & Trial Holes
method_steps.description: CAT & Genny survey of the full working area; hand-dig trial holes to visually confirm depth, material, and position of all gas services before any mechanical plant enters the zone.

method_steps.title: Hand-expose Service
method_steps.description: Hand-excavate to within 0.5m of the gas service; mechanical plant prohibited within this tolerance band.

method_steps.title: Lay & Bed Pipe
method_steps.description: Lay MDPE pipe with correct selected bedding material — minimum 600mm cover on private land, 750mm under adopted highway. Yellow marker tape to be laid 300mm above the crown of the pipe.

method_steps.title: Fusion Jointing
method_steps.description: Electrofusion or butt-fusion joints to be made by MDPE certified operative only; fusion parameters to be recorded on the electrofusion unit datalogger.

method_steps.title: Pressure Test
method_steps.description: Carry out strength and tightness tests in accordance with IGE/UP/1 using nitrogen or compressed air; Gas Safe registered engineer to witness and certify; test records retained.

method_steps.title: Backfill & Compact
method_steps.description: Backfill in 150mm compacted layers using suitable material; compaction plant not to operate directly over live gas service without bridging slabs.

method_steps.title: Reinstatement
method_steps.description: Reinstate road or footway surface to highway authority specification where applicable; retain all dig and reinstatement records.

method_steps.title: Purging & Commissioning
method_steps.description: Gas Safe registered ACS operative to carry out purging and commissioning per IGEM/UP/1B; 4-gas monitor in continuous use; all certificates issued and retained on site.

plant.requirement: Calibration certificate current (max 6 months); bump test carried out each shift before work commences.
Factory calibration current; operator must hold MDPE electrofusion certification; datalogger to record all joint parameters.
For strength testing only — never use natural gas for strength test; cylinder secured and regulators inspected before use.
Calibration certificate to be current; accuracy to be appropriate for the test pressure range.
Operator to be trained in use; batteries checked; CAT and Genny to be used together for live service detection.

coshh.risk: Inhalation of polymer degradation products during electrofusion or butt-fusion welding operations.
coshh.control: RPE FFP2 minimum; forced ventilation in all enclosed spaces; no welding in wet conditions.

competency: Gas Safe registered — appropriate ACS card for work category
NRSWA Street Works Operative qualification (for any highway works)

emergency_procedures.gas_escape: Evacuate area immediately; eliminate all ignition sources; do not operate electrical switches; call 999 and National Gas Emergency Service 0800 111 999; notify principal contractor and site supervisor; do not re-enter until Gas Safe engineer confirms atmosphere clear.
